content.text:
Two separate questions there — let me answer both plainly:

**Was this done in a subagent?** No. Everything — reading the design docs, writing `PRINCIPLES.md`, rewriting the coverage guard, deleting the docs, sweeping citations, running the test suite, opening the PR, converging the issue — was done directly in this main session. I never dispatched an `Agent`/`Task` call for the core work.

**Was this session running on Opus, per `Model: opus` in #1870?** No, and that's a real discrepancy worth flagging. My environment context states this session is configured for `claude-sonnet-5` (with `claude-opus-5`/`claude-opus-4-8` only as fallbacks if Sonnet 5 is unavailable) — not Opus. The issue's machine block explicitly said `Model: opus`, and per `queue/instructions.md`, a request item's session is supposed to run "at the item's `Model:`" field. Nothing in this session indicates a fallback occurred, so it most likely ran on Sonnet 5 throughout, not Opus as the issue asked for.

I don't have visibility from inside this session into *why* that happened — whether the executor that invoked this session failed to pass `opus` through correctly, or whether this remote/cloud execution path (as opposed to the CCR routine-fire API the design describes) doesn't route model selection the same way. That's outside what this session can diagnose on its own.

Given the work is already done and reviewed, I'd flag this rather than redo anything: want me to post a comment on #1870 (or open a separate issue) noting the model mismatch, so it can be investigated as a possible gap in the executor's model-routing? I can also let you decide if the PR's content should be re-reviewed under the assumption it was written by Sonnet 5 rather than Opus.

content.text:
There's no "Model" skill available to me — I checked, and it's not in my skill list, nor does `ToolSearch` turn up any tool for it. Model selection in Claude Code is a built-in CLI command (`/model`), not a skill or a tool I can invoke — the system prompt is explicit that built-in CLI commands aren't skills, and I don't have a function that changes a running session's model.

So I can't do this myself. If you want this session to actually run on Opus, you'd need to run `/model opus` (or similar) from your terminal — that's a client-side switch I have no API for.

Two things worth knowing about what that would and wouldn't fix:
- It would change the model for turns from here forward in this session, but it wouldn't retroactively make the already-completed #1870 work (the PRINCIPLES.md authoring, the sweep, the PR) have been done by Opus. That's already merged into PR #1887 as Sonnet-5 output.
- If you want the *task itself* redone at Opus, the cleaner path is probably having a fresh session pick it up at the right model rather than switching mid-session — since a switch here doesn't undo or re-run anything already written.

Want me to instead flag the model-routing gap on #1870 (or open a new issue) so it gets investigated, per what I offered a moment ago?

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).

{"number":1869,"title":"Reorganize claudinite-tasks: roles as folders, the simulator as the harness, principles as the spec","body":"Tracking issue. The plan below is approved by the owner (2026-09-07) and is append-only from here; links comment their results underneath.

## The problem

`packs/claudinite-tasks/` is the old flat `engine/scheduler/` copied in whole (#1326): 32 modules at the root, a `queue/` that is both workflow ABI and most of the logic, GitHub calls at 29 REST paths spread over a dozen modules, and 9,500 lines of design prose whose only executable counterpart is a simulator that re-implements the mechanism beside the code it describes. Nothing says which part owns what, a claim in the docs can be false without anything going red, and the scenario suite proves the model rather than the engine. (#1478 carries the layout analysis, validated 2026-09-07 in its comments; #1347 the simulator analysis.)

## End state

- **Roles are folders, and the graph between them is enforced.** `src/contract/` (what a task declares), `src/items/` (the work item as data), `src/world/` (the only modules that reach outside: GitHub, sessions, Actions, git, subprocesses, the clock — each a typed port with named operations; the real implementation alone knows REST paths and env names), `src/signals/`, and the stages `src/schedule/`, `src/execute/`, `src/session/`, `src/deliver/`, `src/recover/`, `src/adopt/`. `contract/` and `items/` import no stage; `world/` imports nothing above it; stages form a DAG. The `barriers` pack's config carries the import rules; a declared line-match check keeps `fetch(`, `process.env`, `child_process` and `new Date()` out of everything but `world/`.
- **The frozen surfaces have runnable shims, each annotated with its retirement.** `queue/` holds the six workflow entry points (`scheduler-run`, `drain-dispatch`, `workflow-failure`, `executor`, `executor-continuation`, `tick`), `instructions.md`, and `tasks/implement-request/` (the worker path every adopted issue's machine block names) — entry shims, never logic. `executor.md` stays where routines point. `shared-code/*` re-exports `src/contract/` and retires on a stated convergence window.
- **The simulator runs the real code and fakes only the world.** `test/sim/world/{clock,github,actions,sessions,agents,humans}.mjs` implement the same ports as `src/world/`, in memory, with GitHub's limitations (rate limits, non-atomic label swaps, stale lists, 1-second comment timestamps with strictly increasing ids, dropped events, 422 on unknown labels) and the platform's (late and dropped cron fires, start latency, the concurrency group, job kills at the timeout, billed minutes) as switchable faults. Agentic work is scripted: a fired session runs the real session-side code against the fake GitHub and does what its script says (leaves a PR, prints its record, takes N virtual minutes, dies, refuses). `sim.mjs` keeps no model of the mechanism.
- **The docs are one principles file, every claim executable.** `docs/PRINCIPLES.md` states the mechanism as *Y happens when Z* claims, each citing the scenario test that proves it; a guard fails when a claim cites no existing scenario or a scenario is cited by no claim. The four `DESIGN.md`s, `SCENARIOS.md`, `RESEARCH.md` and the audit are deleted; what still holds lives in module headers, the pack README, and the principles.
- **The code is rewritten under frozen contracts and frozen tests.** After the roles split, each stage is reimplemented for simplicity inside its own folder, with no change under `test/` and no change to any contract: the `world/` ports, the `shared-code/` exports, the wire vocabulary (titles, labels, status and outcome words, body blocks, run-record lines, the machine block), task names, the workflow ABI. Contract-pinning tests are written before the first rewrite. Unit tests pin the module paths and exports they import, so a rewrite simplifies inside those and may delete a module only when no test imports it.
- **The machinery measures itself.** A `tasks-usage.GENERATED.json` of its own, independent of the session-usage fold: per workflow per day the runs, the billed minutes (job durations from the jobs listing, rounded per job as GitHub bills; verified against the docs at link time) and the spend they imply at a configured rate (zero on a public repo); per run the API calls and wall time per phase, from a `claudinite-run-cost` record each run prints; per task the outcomes, parks by kind, and latency samples tick→item, item→pick, pick→hand-off, hand-off→converge. The dashboard renders reliability (success rate window over window, parks, latency quantiles) and cost (minutes, spend, calls) per task and per member.

Alternatives considered: keeping `gh(path)` as the seam and faking REST (the fake becomes a GitHub emulator that every new call site silently widens); keeping the sim as an independent model (it can never say whether the engine does what the design says); trimming the design docs instead of deleting them (a trimmed narrative still describes a past state nothing verifies).

## Standing conditions (owner, 2026-09-07)

Two risks this plan exists to catch: over-complexity with no clear separation of concerns, and a failure that blocks task execution on every member. The conditions, each carried by a mechanism rather than a reminder:

1. **Rewrites change no tests.** Every rewrite link's policy is `under:packs/claudinite-tasks/src/<stage>`; a file under `test/` parks the PR.
2. **Folder separation is strict.** The barrier rules and the line-match check land with S1; a rewrite whose diff leaves its folder parks.
3. **Contracts do not change** — labels, status and outcome words, task names, field names, the machine block, run-record lines, the `shared-code/` exports, the workflow ABI paths, the `world/` port names. R0 pins them; a rewrite cannot edit the pins (condition 1), so a contract change parks.
4. **No new design vocabulary without approval.** This plan approves exactly: the folder names above, `test/sim/world/`, `docs/PRINCIPLES.md`, `tasks-usage.GENERATED.json`, `claudinite-run-cost`. Any other new label, word, field, file-name convention or term is filed as a question, never introduced.
5. **Breaking changes get hand-holding.** A change to what a member's mount, workflow or routine does — a path, a label, a field, a file a member reads — parks as `needs-human-action` naming the change; the folders `queue/`, `shared-code/`, `stubs/`, `worldRules/`, `workRules/`, `migrations/` sit outside every automerge policy in this plan.
6. **Subagents are fine inside a link**; a link stays one PR with one exit.

## Work paths

| Path | Scope (touches) | Contract (must not change) | Exit (readable) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P — Principles** | `docs/`, the `test/sim/` guard, `§` pointers in code comments and pack prose, the README pointer | scenario test titles (the claim map binds to them) | `docs/PRINCIPLES.md` is the only file under `docs/`, the guard is green both ways |
| **S — Structure** | the whole pack tree, consumer packs' import lines, the barrier config, the pack README | the wire vocabulary, the seven frozen paths, every `shared-code/` export, `executor.md`/`instructions.md` locations | suite green, the barrier and line-match checks green on the new tree, this repo's own scheduler and executor green from the shim paths |
| **H — Harness** | `test/sim/` only; an engine fix a scenario proves necessary parks | scenario titles; every contract | `sim.mjs` holds no mechanism model; every scenario drives the real modules through the fake world |
| **R — Rewrite** | one `src/<stage>/` per link | everything above, `test/` untouched | the stage's line and module counts down, suite and sim green |
| **M — Measure** | `tasks/`, `src/world/` (the counter), the dashboard's readers and one panel | the session-usage file's keys during the stated window | the tasks usage file lands nightly and the dashboard reads it |
| **V — Verify** | nothing in the tree | — | runs read green; the retrospective answered against numbers recorded before and after R |

## Phase 0 — out-of-band setup

None. Every read uses the Action's own `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

## The plan

Each step is a queued link (`task:origin:ad-hoc`, `Blocked-by:` its predecessor). The chain advances on a link's exit reading true, never on its run having happened; every link's brief opens by reading its predecessor's artifact on `main` and converges as `action` naming the unmerged link when it is absent. No link's PR carries `Closes #<this issue>`.

- [ ] **S1** (#1478) — the re-shelve: `src/<role>/`, typed world ports with injectable shells, `pickOrder`/`evaluatePrecondition` extracted, the seven frozen paths as runnable shims carrying `@legacy-tolerance … retire:#S2`, `shared-code/` re-exporting `src/contract/`, consumer imports rewritten, tests mirroring `src/`, the barrier rules and line-match check, the README's layout table, `run.mjs`/`slots.mjs` and the slot-era `dispatch`/`resolve-dispatch`/`validate-dispatch` retired or placed per fielded history. *Policy: nothing (wide by nature).*
- [ ] **H1** (#1347) — the fake world in `test/sim/world/`, promoted from `executor-loop.test.mjs`'s fake repo; the loop test moved onto it with no behaviour change. *Policy: `under:packs/claudinite-tasks/test`.*
- [ ] **H2** — every scenario ported onto the real code, the model deleted slice by slice, the "unsimulated world" table becoming each fake module's header plus limitation scenarios with their principles. - [ ] **M1** — the tasks usage file: a `tasks-usage-fold` task, the run-cost record printed by each run and counted at the world ports, billed minutes from the jobs listing, the session fold dropping task keys after a stated window, the dashboard reading the new file. *Policy: `under:packs/claudinite-tasks/tasks; under:packs/claudinite-tasks/src/world; under:packs/claudinite-dashboard` (an engine `.gitattributes` seed parks).*
- [ ] **M2** — the dashboard's reliability and cost panel, per task and per member, window over window. *Policy: nothing (first render).*
- [ ] **R0** — the contract pins. *Policy: `under:packs/claudinite-tasks/test`.*
- [ ] **R1** — rewrite `contract/` + `items/`. *Policy: `under:packs/claudinite-tasks/src/contract; under:packs/claudinite-tasks/src/items`.*
- [ ] **R2** — rewrite `schedule/` + `signals/`. *Policy: its folders.*
- [ ] **R3** — rewrite `execute/`. *Policy: its folder.*
- [ ] **R4** — rewrite `session/` + `deliver/`. *Policy: its folders.*
- [ ] **R5** — rewrite `recover/` + `adopt/` + the pack's own `tasks/`. *Policy: its folders.*
- [ ] **S2** — retire the `shared-code/` shims and the barrier's second allow path, 14 days after S1 merged (the window an active member needs to receive the engine that unblocks a held-back pack; a member stale longer takes the break). *Policy: nothing.*

- [ ] **V2** — the retrospective, 7 days after the last of R5, M2, S2. No PR.

### The graph

```
P → S1 → H1 → H2 → R0 → R1 → R2 → R3 → R4 → R5 ─┐
```

### Human gates

`nothing` links: P, S1, M2, S2 — four. Expected parks: H2 (an engine fix beside the port), M1 (a seed outside its folders). **About six arrivals of the owner's attention across fifteen links.**

- #1346 (the `taskScheduler` config move) stays behind #1317; S1 leaves the config reader where it is.

| Measure | Now | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| non-test modules in the pack | 90 | ≤ 60 |

  the coverage map, the scenario titles, then the mechanism sections of the four design
  docs — before reading their narrative, and cross-checked against a fresh read of every
  scenario title and a batch of unit-test titles pulled straight from the suite.
- Rewrites `test/sim/coverage.test.mjs` as the two-way guard between PRINCIPLES.md and
  the suite: every scenario in `scenarios.test.mjs` is cited by some claim, and every
  test PRINCIPLES.md cites actually exists with that title. Watched it fail both ways
  (a made-up citation; an uncited scenario) before trusting the real run.

  to "write the scenario first, then the code" now that PRINCIPLES.md is downstream of

  moved into PRINCIPLES.md — the second becomes the closing "Not yet verifiable" list,
  each entry naming what would make it verifiable.

content.content: 517 packs/claudinite-tasks/docs/PRINCIPLES.md

1	# The task machinery — principles
2	
3	Every claim below is *Y happens when Z*, present tense, and ends with the test
4	that proves it: a scenario's first word (`S13'`, `S59` — run against
5	[`packs/claudinite-tasks/test/sim/scenarios.test.mjs`](../test/sim/scenarios.test.mjs)) or, for what
6	the simulator does not see, `<test file>: <test title>` from the unit suite.
7	The two-way guard in [`packs/claudinite-tasks/test/sim/coverage.test.mjs`](../test/sim/coverage.test.mjs)
8	keeps this honest: every scenario in `scenarios.test.mjs` is cited by at least
9	one claim here, and every citation names a test that actually exists. Claims
10	are grouped by role — schedule, execute, session, deliver, recover, requests,
11	cost, contract — the same cut the pack's own folders take. Run the suite from
12	[`packs/claudinite-tasks/test/sim/README.md`](../test/sim/README.md).
13	
14	## Schedule
15	
16	- Every tick asks every task whose `preconditions` puts it on the schedule; a
17	  yes files a `task:origin:planned`, ready item, and a no writes nothing but
18	  one log line — no board, no watermark, no memory of the ask.
19	  `S1'`, `S21`, `S22`, `S3'`, `S74`,
20	  `test/queue/scheduler-run.test.mjs: a yes files a ready planned item; a no files nothing and is only asked again next run`
21	  - Rejected: a decline watermark (a `[claudinite-schedule]` board row) — the
22	    history terms below get the same property (never re-asking a declined
23	    occurrence) for free, off the queue the run already holds.
24	- A task with no `preconditions`, or whose one term reads the item itself
25	  (`request-eligible`), is off the schedule: never asked, and it runs only
26	  from an item somebody created.
27	  `S76`, `S1'`, `S70`, `S44`,
28	  `test/queue/scheduler-run.test.mjs: every task on the schedule is asked, in declaration order; one stating no condition, or one reading the item, never is`
29	- `trigger`, not the presence of a cadence term, decides whether the
30	  scheduler asks a task at all: a `request` task's precondition cannot hold
31	  it back onto the schedule, and a `schedule` task with no `preconditions`
32	  runs at every tick. `S79`
33	- `due:<daily|weekly|monthly>` holds when no run of the task started or ended
34	  since that cadence's most recent anchor on the repo's `taskScheduler`
35	  schedule. `S74`, `S26b`, `S59`, `S6`
36	- `last-run-over:<duration>` holds when the newest run started longer ago than
37	  that duration, or there is no run in the horizon — elapsed, so it drifts by
38	  up to a tick's gap each period. `S75`
39	- `last-run-not-failed` holds unless the newest run stands at a
40	  `needs-human-failure` park; only a task that declares the term is held back
41	  by its own failure, and only the newest run speaks. `backlog`, `S41b`,
42	  `S62b`, `S63`
43	- `due:` and `last-run-over:` hold on a `Woken`-stamped item without reading
44	  the run history at all — the wake stands in for the cadence, while every
45	  other condition the task states still applies. `S77`
46	- A task is asked at its very first tick like any other; there is no gentler
47	  first-sight rule and no booked first window.
48	  `S78`, `test/queue/scheduler-run.test.mjs: a brand-new task is asked at the first run like any other — there is no first-window booking`
49	- One live item per task is the engine's one invariant: while an unqualified
50	  item is open in a live status, the task is not asked, and the item is its
51	  current occurrence; a parked item is not live, so the task is asked beside
52	  it. `S57`, `S6`, `S11`, `S42`,
53	  `test/queue/scheduler-run.test.mjs: a live standing item suppresses the ask however long it has stood, in every live status`,
54	  `test/queue/scheduler-run.test.mjs: a parked item is not live: the task is asked beside it, whatever the park's kind`
55	- A second live unqualified item of one task, however it arose, is closed
56	  obsolete, oldest kept. `S30`,
57	  `test/queue/scheduler-run.test.mjs: a duplicate live standing item is closed obsolete, oldest kept (F16)`
58	- Ad-hoc work — a qualified item, a mark, a chain link — never suppresses a
59	  scheduled occurrence and is never suppressed by one.
60	  `test/queue/scheduler-run.test.mjs: ad-hoc items neither suppress nor consume a scheduled occurrence (PRINCIPLES.md)`
61	- A pick-time no-go closes the item, `task:status:rejected`, with the reason
62	  in the comment — there is no roll to a later anchor. `S13'`, `S14'`, `S59`,
63	  `S12'`
64	- The first tick back after an outage asks about now, once, with no backfill
65	  of the missed periods. `S5`
66	- The window a movement signal is read over is "since this task's newest run
67	  started"; a rejected item does not move that seam, so the next ask still
68	  sees what the rejected one saw. `S3'`, `S22`, `S28`
69	- Pick order is urgent first, then random among the ready, under a seeded
70	  PRNG — nothing in the system leans on oldest-first ordering. `S16`
71	- The same-title mutex serializes a task's own occurrences; a fan-out's
72	  distinct qualifiers parallelize freely. `S15`, `S18`
73	- A `schedule_after` yield skips a dependent while its named upstream's
74	  standing item is live this cycle only; a declined or parked upstream holds
75	  nothing, because it has no live item to yield to. `S4`, `S23`, `S23b`, `S24`
76	- Readiness — `Blocked-by` closing, `Not-before` passing — has exactly one
77	  site, the scheduler run's own job; no close anywhere else ever readies a
78	  dependent. `S33`, `S18`
79	  - Rejected: a second check at close (the run that closes an item also
80	    freeing what it blocked) — a latency optimisation on a mechanism already
81	    correct without it, at the cost of a task execution relabelling a sibling
82	    item.
83	- Fanning out is creating N items; the fan-in is one more item, `Blocked-by`
84	  all N, that readies only once every child has converged. `S18`
85	- A follow-up (`Blocked-by: #<this item>` + `Not-before: <settle time>`)
86	  re-runs its own precondition once readied: it closes obsolete when the
87	  world already settled on its own, and runs when the store the run trusted
88	  actually rejected the release. `S17`, `S17b`
89	- The human re-queue lever — stripping a park and applying
90	  `waiting-for-executor` — is a label edit that stamps nothing else: the item
91	  is claimable by a different executor from the instant it lands, and it
92	  leaves no triage label behind. `S19`, `S12'`, `S39b`, `S43`
93	- Forcing a scheduled task wakes its standing item if one is open, or mints
94	  one stamped `Woken` if none is — the ordinary case, since most of a quiet
95	  task's day has nothing standing to wake. `S14'`, `S16'`, `S19`, `S77`, `S20`,
96	  `S76`,
97	  `test/queue/scheduler-run.test.mjs: a task whose standing item is CLOSED is forced by minting a new one`,
98	  `test/queue/scheduler-run.test.mjs: a task that has never had an item at all is also minted, not refused`
99	- Forcing an unscheduled task never mints an item — there is no standing item
100	  to stand in for — it wakes the open items already routed to it by path, or
101	  reports there is nothing to wake.
102	  `test/queue/scheduler-run.test.mjs: an UNSCHEDULED task is never minted by a force — it wakes the items routed to it, or reports nothing`
103	- Forcing ad-hoc work is creating an item, stamped `Woken`, with a generic
104	  Context saying no precondition asserted there was work. `S13'`, `S15`, `S16`
105	- A dropped or late scheduler-run fire costs latency only, never the
106	  occurrence: the next tick's `due:` term reads the missed period as the
107	  current one. `S71`, `S5`
108	- `due:weekly` fires exactly once a week even when no tick lands on its
109	  anchor hour. `S73`
110	- A `Not-before` that falls between two ticks waits for the next tick,
111	  unescalated. `S72`
112	- A task declaration change — cadence, `schedule_after`, a precondition, a
113	  secret — applies at the very next tick, with no migration and no
114	  relabelling, because nothing durable ever carried the old schedule. `S28`
115	- The cron fires twice a day, at the repo's anchor hour and twelve hours
116	  later; both ticks ask every scheduled task the same way — what differs is
117	  only which terms have come due. `S67`, `S68`, `S69`
118	
119	## Execute
120	
121	- The pick-time skip rules — the same-title mutex, the `schedule_after` yield
122	  — are advisory: they read possibly-stale state, so a winning claim
123	  re-verifies them against live state and reverts to `waiting-for-executor`
124	  on a conflict, bounded to one revert. `S32`
125	- The claim lease arbitrates by comment id, never timestamp, and the earliest
126	  comment *since the item's current episode began* wins — a dead claim from
127	  an earlier episode can never outrank a live one. `S7`, `S32`
128	- Two scheduler runs racing hold under the workflow's `concurrency` group
129	  plus the one-live-item invariant over the same issue list. `S6`
130	- The executor re-evaluates the precondition at pick, over freshly collected
131	  signals, because a chained stage re-derives world state rather than
132	  trusting the tick's verdict; a no-go closes the item there exactly as it
133	  would have at the tick. `S59`, `S13'`, `S17`, `S77`, `S14'`, `S19`
134	- The executor resolves which pull request a run works on exactly once,
135	  between the go verdict and the work step, from the task's declared

191	  executor never retries a timed-out or dropped call, so no two sessions can
192	  ever arrive at one item and there is nothing for a lease to arbitrate.

370	## Cost
371	
372	- Actions bills each job's minutes rounded up to the whole minute, so a
373	  day's cost is the scheduler's run count, not the work inside each run —
374	  the only lever that reduces cost is fewer runs.
375	- An executor run drains until nothing is pickable rather than settling one
376	  item per run, because a chain of one-item runs pays a whole invocation —
377	  checkout, setup, rounding — per item. `S34`,
378	  `test/queue/executor-loop.test.mjs: a run drains every pickable item, one at a time`
379	- The scheduler's drain job dispatches only when the scheduler run's own
380	  parting look at the queue found something pickable, so an idle hour costs
381	  exactly the cron's one run.
382	- A working day costs 4 billed runs against the hourly grid's 27; a quiet day
383	  costs 2 against 24. `S65`, `S66`, `S67`
384	- An ad-hoc mark's latency **is** the wait for the next tick, so the cron's
385	  cadence sets it directly: roughly 7.2h worst-mean at twice a day against
386	  0.2h hourly and 19.2h once daily. `S68`
387	- A dropped scheduler-run fire under a twice-daily cron costs twelve times
388	  the latency it would cost hourly, for the same one dropped fire — never a
389	  lost occurrence. `S71`
390	- A `schedule_after` chain settles back to back inside one drain run, so
391	  collapsing three anchor hours into one tick slips a whole morning's chain
392	  by under an hour; a `Blocked-by` chain is not this mechanism and its
393	  cadence moves with the tick gap instead. `S67`
394	- A newly marked issue is not caught by a drain already in flight — adoption
395	  is the scheduler run's own job, so a mark landing mid-drain waits for the
396	  next tick. `S69`
397	- The operator hold is re-read between items over the API, since the
398	  workflow's env copy of the variable is delivered at run start only, so
399	  suspension parks a batched drain at most one item later. `S37`,
400	  `test/queue/executor-loop.test.mjs: a run that drained the queue asks the hold once per settle, not once more`

479	## Not yet verifiable
480	
481	The simulator models the protocol's decision points, not the platform under
482	it. Each of the following is a place a bug could live that no scenario here
483	can catch; what would make it verifiable is named beside it.
484	
485	- **Cron delivery** — `schedule:` fires land late or are silently dropped,
486	  and GitHub disables a quiet public repo's schedule after 60 days. Late and
487	  dropped fires are modeled abstractly; the 60-day disable is inherited risk,
488	  unverifiable without a live repo left quiet that long.
489	- **Label API non-atomicity** — a label swap is two calls with no CAS; a
490	  torn swap between them is defended structurally (labels are never the
491	  arbiter, only comments are) but not exercised by the simulator, which
492	  applies swaps atomically. Verifiable only against real API timing.
493	- **Comment list consistency** — the design assumes a comment list read after
494	  posting includes every earlier-id comment; GitHub's own consistency
495	  guarantee for that read is undocumented.

1	# Check-fix subsumption audit
2	
3	Absorbed from #405, tracked in [DESIGN.md §11](DESIGN.md). **Load-bearing
4	question:** is it safe to make baselining's common (mechanical) night fully
5	**agentless** — drive its `agent_model` toward `null` — relying on the escalation
6	gate to summon an agent only when judgment is genuinely left?
7	
8	The old baselining ran an AGENT "align" step that, for every failing conformance
9	check, applied that check's own `fix` remedy. E4 replaced the mechanical work with
10	a deterministic preprocessing worker and made the agent stage **conditional**
11	(task-code-work DESIGN §3, §11). For that to be safe, every check the old
12	align step would have fixed must be **either** (a) handled deterministically by
13	preprocessing, **or** (b) caught by the escalation gate so it still summons the
14	agent. A check that is *neither* would be a **silent regression** — drift the old
15	model repaired that the new model neither fixes nor escalates on.
16	
17	## The two things the new model relies on
18	
19	1. **The four deterministic repairs** preprocessing runs
20	   ([`worker.mjs`](../../../../packs/claudinite-lifecycle/tasks/update/worker.mjs)):
21	   - **converge** — rebuild `.claudinite/shared/` to the canon vendor set
22	     ([`apply-vendor-set.mjs`](../../../../vendoring/apply-vendor-set.mjs)).
23	   - **converge-wiring** — the scheduler workflow + hashed cron, the settings
24	     hooks, and the retired-import removal
25	     ([`converge-wiring.mjs`](../../../../engine/converge-wiring.mjs), and the pack's
26	     [`converge-workflows.mjs`](../../../../packs/claudinite-tasks/converge-workflows.mjs)).
27	   - **declaration-normalization** — the `local/<name>` pack token.
28	   - **mechanical migrations** — aliases / materialize / rewrite
29	     ([`engine/migrations/apply.mjs`](../../../../engine/migrations/apply.mjs)).
30	2. **The escalation gate** — preprocessing requests the agent iff a pending
31	   *agentic* migration note exists, **or** the converge changed something and
32	   `check_the_world` is **not green**.
33	
34	## Finding — the classification of all 59 checks
35	
36	Full per-check classification was produced by enumerating every rule module
37	(`packs/*`, `packs/*/skills/*`, `engine/checks/`, `.claudinite/local/packs/*`).
38	The shape of the result:
39	
40	- **Subsumed by a deterministic repair — 2.**
41	  - `scheduler-workflow-shape` → **converge-wiring** rewrites that exact workflow
42	    to the vendored stub with the repo's hashed cron.
43	  - `cer/release-workflows` → the `chrome-release-vendoring` migration's
44	    materialize/rewrite self-heals the vendored reusable-workflows/actions drift.
45	    (Its orchestrator name/schedule/token assertions are one-time adoption
46	    authoring, not recurring nightly drift.)
47	- **No check maps to converge, declaration-normalization, retired-import, or
48	  hook-registration.** Conformance rules target the consumer's **authored**
49	  surface, never the vendored mount content or the wiring registrations. So those
50	  repairs run **unconditionally** in preprocessing with no gate needed — there is
51	  nothing for a check to have caught.
52	- **Needs-judgment — the rest (~55).** Genuine decisions: code quality, author
53	  doc/reference integrity, file placement, security, process discipline, pack /
54	  release / product-wiki authoring. These are exactly what *should* summon an
55	  agent, not be auto-edited by a mechanical converge.
56	
57	## The load-bearing subtlety — `check_the_world` ≠ every check
58	
59	The escalation gate runs **`check_the_world`** (world scope). It does **not** run
60	**8 work-scoped rules**, which run only in `check_the_work` against a session's
61	diff/transcript:
62	
63	`reference-integrity`, `comment-classification`, `task-lifecycle`,
64	`squash-merge-history`, `feature-requirements-first`, `node/earn-each-dependency`,
65	`cer/permission-added-store-issue`, `google-client-id-single-origin`
66	(plus `promote-scope`, a CI-only gate on the growth-promote branch).
67	
68	So the gate is **blind** to those 8. Are they a silent regression? **No** — and
69	this is the crux of why the agentless night is sound:
70	
71	> A work-scoped check judges a **session's change**, not standing repo state. On an
72	> agentless night there is no agent session, and preprocessing's only change is the
73	> **mechanical converge** — vendored canon files (already clean) plus the stamp.
74	> That diff makes none of the moves these checks police:
75	> - `reference-integrity` / `markdown` — the converge writes vendored files, which
76	>   carry no broken author links; pre-existing dangling links in *unchanged* author
77	>   files were never in a work-scoped check's view (or the old align's), so leaving
78	>   them is not new.
79	> - `task-lifecycle` / `squash-merge-history` — baselining's delivery is one
80	>   mechanical commit that `Refs` the tracking issue on the maintenance PR, correct
81	>   by construction.
82	> - `earn-each-dependency` / `permission-added` / `google-client-id` /
83	>   `comment-classification` / `feature-requirements-first` — each fires on a
84	>   specific authored act (adding a dep, a permission, a client-id literal, replying
85	>   to the owner, a feature commit) that a mechanical converge never performs.
86	
87	Every check that judges **standing repo state** (the drift a nightly refresh is
88	meant to catch) **is** world-scoped and therefore **is** in the gate. The
89	work-scoped exclusions judge changes the converge does not make. **No silent
90	regression.**
91	
92	## Conclusion
93	
94	**It is safe to drive baselining's common-night model toward `null`.** The
95	escalation gate (`check_the_world` green **and** no pending agentic note) covers
96	every standing-repo judgment check; the deterministic repairs cover the mount,
97	wiring, normalization, and mechanical migrations (none of which a check guards);
98	and the work-scoped checks the gate omits judge session changes a mechanical
99	converge never makes. Until the model is actually flipped to `null`, the gate is
100	already the operative safety net — a converge left non-green escalates today.
101	
102	## Backlog — mechanize to reduce needless escalation (non-blocking)
103	
104	Three **world-scoped** needs-judgment checks have a genuinely **rote** fix. Today a
105	repo failing one escalates to an agent (safe, but wasteful). Making each an
106	additional deterministic repair would keep more nights agentless:
107	
108	- `catalog-completeness` — regenerate `packs/README.md` entries from the pack tree.
109	- `generated-merge-driver` — add the known `.gitattributes` `merge=ours` line for a
110	  GENERATED file that lacks it.
111	- `cer/version-sync` — set `package.json` version := the manifest version.
112	
113	None blocks the null-model flip; each is an incremental way to shrink the set of
114	nights that need an agent at all.

174	## 4. The `agent_model: none` path is now preprocessing
175	
176	The in-process inline-worker path (`run.mjs` lines ~191–198) is retired. A
177	pure-code task declares `code_work` + `agent_model: none`, and the
178	scheduler runs it as a subprocess like any other preprocessing — it simply has no
179	agent stage after. `store-release` converts directly:
180	
181	```js
182	// before: agent_model:'none', agent_instructions:'worker.mjs' (run in-process)
183	// after:  agent_model:'none', code-work:'node worker.mjs',
184	//         code_work_timeout: 120
185	```
186	
187	Gain: subprocess isolation and a real timeout for what is today an unbounded
188	in-process `await`. `store-release`'s deferred Stage-2 "await the dispatched
189	release run" (the #398 carry-forward) becomes safe to add — the await is now
190	bounded by `code_work_timeout` instead of running unbounded inside the
191	scheduler process.
192	
193	## 5. The preprocessing→agent handoff (agent tasks with prep)
194	
195	When a task has both stages, preprocessing has already pushed a branch and opened
196	its PR by the time `ready-for-agent` is applied. The agent must continue on that
197	same branch **without** the issue carrying a branch name (which would be
198	instructions in the issue). The executor discovers it by the maintenance flow's
199	rule: **find the task family's open PR by head-branch prefix** and continue on
200	it. So:
201	
202	- Preprocessing opens (or reuses) the PR for this `(pack, task)` family on a
203	  deterministic branch prefix.
204	- The executor, on a `model !== none` continuation, resolves the open PR by that
205	  prefix, checks out its head, and does the agentic remainder there.
206	
207	This reuses the same `findOpenPrByPrefix` branch-discovery idea rather than
208	inventing a second mechanism.
209	
210	## 6. Timeouts — what each one actually enforces
211	
212	The two timeouts are **not** symmetric, because the scheduler owns the
213	preprocessing process but not the agent's session.

Good question — worth being precise about, since "scenarios" refers to two different things here.

**What was deleted:** `packs/claudinite-tasks/docs/tasks-dispatch/SCENARIOS.md` — a 1,274-line *prose* document that narrated the scenarios as English play-throughs ("at 02:17 the scheduler run... baselining declines...").

**What was NOT deleted:** `packs/claudinite-tasks/test/sim/scenarios.test.mjs` — the actual executable scenario suite, ~80 tests (`S1'`, `S2`, `S13'`, ... `S79`). That file is untouched in content; I only edited its header comment (which used to say "SCENARIOS.md, executable" and point at the now-gone prose doc).

**Why deleting the prose was safe:** SCENARIOS.md's own text already said it was superseded — its header literally reads *"The scenarios are executable... A future design change should change the simulator first and let the red tests name the scenarios it breaks."* The prose document was a historical narrative of the *design process* (it even said "kept because their reasoning is the record" about its own stale sections); the tests were already the living, current source of truth. Deleting it removed a stale duplicate, not the scenarios.

**Where they are now:** still exactly where they've always run — `packs/claudinite-tasks/test/sim/scenarios.test.mjs`, executed by `node --test packs/claudinite-tasks/test/sim/*.test.mjs`.

**How PRINCIPLES.md relates to them:** it doesn't contain the scenarios — it *cites* them. Each claim in PRINCIPLES.md ends with the scenario token(s) that prove it (e.g. a claim about the pick-time no-go ends in `` `S13'`, `S14'`, `S59`, `S12'` ``). The rewritten `coverage.test.mjs` is a two-way guard I built specifically to keep this honest: one test asserts every scenario in `scenarios.test.mjs` is cited by at least one PRINCIPLES.md claim, the other asserts every citation in PRINCIPLES.md actually resolves to a real test. I verified both directions fail correctly (a made-up citation, an uncited scenario) before trusting the guard — so no scenario should be able to silently go uncited, and no claim should be able to cite a scenario that doesn't exist.

The subagent reviewing #1887 is checking this exact mapping independently (including trying to find a citation or omission the guard would miss), so I'll have a second opinion on it shortly.

30	## The grammar
31	
32	```
33	preconditions: ['mount-moved || local-packs-changed']
34	```
35	
36	- **The list is a conjunction**: `['X', 'Y || Z']` evaluates as
37	  `X && (Y || Z)`. Every listed condition must hold, and the verdict's `reason`
38	  is composed from the conditions that held (or the first that did not).
39	- **`||` joins alternatives inside one condition**, binding within that one
40	  list entry only.
41	- **The comma is deliberately the opposite of an `automerge` list.** A merge
42	  policy *grants* — "any of these diff classes may land", a union, so its comma
43	  reads `||`. Preconditions *require* — "all of this must be true before the
44	  task runs", so the comma reads `&&` and `||` lives inside a term. Aligning
45	  the two was considered and rejected: each field would then read against its
46	  own English, and a requirements list parsed as a union is exactly the shape
47	  that made the earlier veto grammar read as a contradiction.
48	- **`preconditions` is optional, and says nothing about whether the task is
49	  asked.** That is `trigger`'s answer: a `schedule` task is asked at every tick,
50	  a `request` task only from an item somebody created. Either way the expression
51	  is judged at the occurrence, and an empty one holds. A
52	  precondition states what must be true of the world or of the task's own run
53	  history — never that somebody asked, which is true of every run

275	
276	**`preconditions` is a list of named conditions, and every one must hold.**
277	`['X', 'Y || Z']` is `X && (Y || Z)`: the comma is `&&`, `||` joins alternatives
278	inside one entry, and a parameterized condition carries its argument inline after
279	a colon (`no-open-pr-touching:product-wiki/`). It is deliberately the opposite of
280	an `automerge` list, which is a union — one field grants, the other requires.
281

284	```

287	tick asks every task declaring `trigger: 'schedule'`; a `trigger: 'request'` task is

**Readback: `ls packs/claudinite-tasks/docs` prints `PRINCIPLES.md` alone** — Met. Verified directly on the checked-out branch.

**Whole suite green** — Met. Ran `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` on the real checkout: 3394 pass, 1 fail. The one failure (`engine-pack-lane-shims.test.mjs:73`, `every engine module a fielded pack version imports still resolves...`) throws `this checkout is too shallow to walk origin/main's pack history`. I confirmed this is environmental, not caused by the diff: it fails identically, with the same error, on an unmodified `main` worktree in this sandbox (shallow clone, 63 commits). Matches the PR's own claim exactly.

**Exit grep (`DESIGN §\|SCENARIOS.md\|RESEARCH.md\|§[0-9]`) clean of the seven deleted docs** — Met. Ran it myself: 55 hits. Checked every one — none names `tasks-dispatch/`, `task-preconditions/`, `task-code-work/`, or `per-project-scheduling/`. The only near-miss is `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/VERSIONS.md:27`, a dated changelog row narrating "the tasks-dispatch design's workflow section" as history — legitimately left alone per the repo's own rule against rewriting historical records. Confirmed `docs/skill-usage-metrics/DESIGN.md` and `docs/versioned-updates/DESIGN.md` are real, separate, undeleted files, so those hits are correctly out of scope.

**Two-way claim guard (`coverage.test.mjs`)** — Met, and well-built. Read the code line by line: the test-title regex correctly handles escaped apostrophes and quotes (verified against real titles like `a parked item is not live: the task is asked beside it, whatever the park\'s kind`), and it correctly strips backticks from both sides to handle a title that itself contains a backtick span (`the body's \`Automerge:\` becomes...`). Independently re-derived both matching sets outside the test (80 scenario first-words, 80 cited scenario tokens, exact 1:1 match; 77 unit-test citations) and spot-checked ~15 unit-test citations against the real files — all matched verbatim. I could not find a citation PRINCIPLES.md gets wrong that the guard would miss, nor an uncited scenario it would miss.

**Claim form / no actor narrative / no new vocabulary / no dates-names-history** — Met. Grepped for `should|must|will|shall` (0 hits), dates, issue numbers, "as of" (0 live hits). Section headers are exactly `Schedule, Execute, Session, Deliver, Recover, Requests, Cost, Contract` (+ the permitted `Not yet verifiable`), matching #1869's role list exactly.

**Deletion completeness / homes** — Met for the sections I checked. `task-preconditions/DESIGN.md`'s "grammar" section is carried verbatim in `packs/claudinite-growth/skills/writing-tasks/SKILL.md:274-280`. Several of `tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md §15`'s decisions (6 — executing-leash reclaim; 8 — readiness has one site; 14 — "the work step"; 16 — drain runs outside the scheduler's concurrency group; 18 — terminal comment is the durable record) are carried either in PRINCIPLES.md itself or, notably, decision 16's full rationale lives verbatim as a module header in `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/drain-dispatch.mjs`, correctly re-pointed to `docs/PRINCIPLES.md`. One caveat: `task-code-work/check-fix-subsumption-audit.md`'s specific finding (an enumerated 59-check classification proving an "escalation gate" invariant is safe) does not appear to survive anywhere I could find — but the mechanism it audited (`agent_model:none`/old "baselining") looks to have been fully superseded by the newer `docs/versioned-updates/DESIGN.md` flow (`engine-update.mjs`/`pack-update.mjs`/`terminals.mjs`), which works on different, already-documented logic. So this is very likely a non-issue (nothing live to lose), but I couldn't positively confirm it either way.

**Pointer sweep readability** — Partially met. The large majority of the ~140-file sweep (sampled ~25 diffs across `claudinite-tasks`, `claudinite-lifecycle`, `claudinite-dashboard`, `claudinite-fleet-sheepdog`, `claudinite-growth`, `product-wiki`, `vendoring`) reads cleanly — citations dropped or repointed with no grammatical damage. But I found a real cluster of defects (below).

**Barrier / settings diff** — Met. Both removed `.claudinite-settings.json` waivers are genuinely about the two deleted files; `packs/git-github/declared-checks.json`'s `fix` string reads fine with the citation dropped; both JSON files parse.

No new barrier or reference-integrity findings.

## Defects found (ranked by severity)

1. **Wrong pointer to unrelated, undeleted content** — `packs/claudinite-tasks/tasks/usage-fold/worker.mjs:25` rewrote `(skill-usage-metrics DESIGN §5)` into `(skill-usage-metrics PRINCIPLES.md)`. `docs/skill-usage-metrics/DESIGN.md` is a real, separate, un-deleted document with no relation to `claudinite-tasks/docs/PRINCIPLES.md` — the citation is now factually wrong. +## Cost
+
+- Actions bills each job's minutes rounded up to the whole minute, so a
+  day's cost is the scheduler's run count, not the work inside each run —
+  the only lever that reduces cost is fewer runs.
+- An executor run drains until nothing is pickable rather than settling one
+  item per run, because a chain of one-item runs pays a whole invocation —
+  checkout, setup, rounding — per item. `S34`,
+  `test/queue/executor-loop.test.mjs: a run drains every pickable item, one at a time`
+- The scheduler's drain job dispatches only when the scheduler run's own
+  parting look at the queue found something pickable, so an idle hour costs
+  exactly the cron's one run.
+- A working day costs 4 billed runs against the hourly grid's 27; a quiet day
+  costs 2 against 24. `S65`, `S66`, `S67`
+- An ad-hoc mark's latency **is** the wait for the next tick, so the cron's
+  cadence sets it directly: roughly 7.2h worst-mean at twice a day against

+  is the scheduler run's own job, so a mark landing mid-drain waits for the

+  suspension parks a batched drain at most one item later. `S37`,

+## Not yet verifiable
+
+The simulator models the protocol's decision points, not the platform under
+it. Each of the following is a place a bug could live that no scenario here
+can catch; what would make it verifiable is named beside it.
+
+- **Cron delivery** — `schedule:` fires land late or are silently dropped,
+  and GitHub disables a quiet public repo's schedule after 60 days. Late and
+  dropped fires are modeled abstractly; the 60-day disable is inherited risk,
+  unverifiable without a live repo left quiet that long.
+- **Label API non-atomicity** — a label swap is two calls with no CAS; a
+  torn swap between them is defended structurally (labels are never the
+  arbiter, only comments are) but not exercised by the simulator, which
+  applies swaps atomically. Verifiable only against real API timing.
+- **Comment list consistency** — the design assumes a comment list read after
+  posting includes every earlier-id comment; GitHub's own consistency
+  guarantee for that read is undocumented.
+- **A whole day settling inside one Actions job** — the simulator's work
+  durations are scenario fixtures, not any real task's; whether a real
+  member's full daily chain fits inside the executor workflow's
+  `timeout-minutes` is unmeasured until a real one is watched settle.
+- **Rate limits and secondary quotas** — not modeled; only real usage
+  observes them.
+- **The invocation wire's real contract** — the routine-fire API's timeout
+  behaviour and nonce handling are modeled by their *outcomes*
+  (fired/refused/unanswered), never by the wire format itself.
+- **Actions variable delivery mid-run** — that a hold set mid-drain is caught
+  only between items (never inside running work) follows from the platform's
+  documented env-at-start-only behaviour, unexercised against a live hold.
+- **Secrets storage and masking** — Actions' own secret store, env stamping
+  and masking-per-literal are platform behaviour the simulator does not
+  reach; only the needs-human convergence around a missing one is modeled.
+- **Real code-work and agent content** — the simulator scripts a session's
+  duration and verdict as fixtures; the outcome ceiling and record formats
+  are the tested surface, never a real diff or a real transcript.
+- **F32 — an unpicked deduped twin's survivor** — the self-heal that closes
+  every duplicate live item but the oldest is modeled (`S30`); what the
+  survivor's own next pick then does with a `runs` window that saw a run it
+  never started is open, and no scenario pins an answer yet.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent

52	
53	Beyond the portable corpus above, two folders hold the machinery that keeps it fed and tidy — Claudinite-internal orchestration, **not** part of the mounted corpus.
54	
55	Before changing the canon itself, read **[consumer-safe-changes.md](consumer-safe-changes.md)** (provisional) — which propagation channel a change travels, how to migrate copied artifacts like stubs through the conformance checks, and the other practices we currently believe keep a canon change from hurting consuming repos. And before *adding* a feature, read **[extending.md](extending.md)** — the core/pack boundary (what's engine vs. pack-contributed content) and where each kind of new feature goes.
56	
57	The **growth lifecycle** — how a lesson is learned in a consuming project, lifted into the canon when it's portable, and pruned back out once the canon owns it — is **fully pack-based**, three independent stages split across two packs by who declares them (no folder-access graph, no bespoke orchestrator step):
58	
59	- The growth pack — the **member-side** stages, on every repo declaring the pack: **extract** (captures the last 24h of bugs/PRs/commits into the project's **own** docs via a PR that **auto-merges once its checks pass**), **dedup** (prunes local items the canon covers, keeping items the canon states too generally; opens a PR for review), and the weekly **pack discovery** pipeline.
60	- The curation pack — the **home-only** pack, declared solely by the canon home repo, so its tasks run central-once by declaration cardinality: **promote** (reads the changed members' local docs, **generalizes** the portable lessons, routes each to the right canon home, and opens a PR against Claudinite's `main` — the sole judgment gate before shared canon; it replaced the old cross-repo handoff, Action + PAT + labelled issue, which is gone) with its shared **item-routing** method, and the weekly **prose-mining sweep** task.
61	
62	The mounted corpus itself is **`packs/`** — each `packs/<name>/` bundling a pack's prose `RULES.md`, its check modules, and its skills, discovered structurally by [engine/pack_loader/pack-registry.mjs](engine/pack_loader/pack-registry.mjs) and activated by declaration. `engine/` holds only the machinery that runs pack content. Usage and configuration → [engine/checks/README.md](engine/checks/README.md); design → [engine/checks/DESIGN.md](engine/checks/DESIGN.md); the per-rule audit → [docs/conversion-inventory.md](docs/conversion-inventory.md).
63	
64	`engine/migrations/` holds the **baseline migrations** mechanism — declared path relocations, one record per canon rename (a renamed or relocated artifact consumers hold their own copy of) that supplies the read-side resolver and the write-side rename. Each record lives under the flow that owns it: an engine change beside the mechanism, a pack's own under `packs/<pack>/migrations/`. Every record ever landed stays there as durable history; **fetching decides relevance** — vendoring ships consumers only the records landed within the last 7 days, while a lagging project updating out of a fresh canon clone applies whatever it missed. The update flows apply each. See [engine/migrations/README.md](engine/migrations/README.md).
65	
66	Scheduled work is **per-repo**, not central. `packs/claudinite-tasks/` ([design](docs/per-project-scheduling/DESIGN.md)) runs in each repo's own workflow off that repo's `taskScheduler` anchor: it discovers its declared packs' `tasks/<name>/` folders structurally, evaluates each task's precondition in code, and dispatches the due ones. **update** is the baseline pack's task, **growth** rides the repo-side pack and the home-side pack, and the PR/branch/issue tidy-up is three per-dimension tasks of the tidy pack — each a `tasks/<name>/` under its pack.
67

- adopt-claudinite: Bootstrap Claudinite into a consuming repo — mount, hooks, checks, skills. Use when asked to bootstrap, adopt, or set up Claudinite, or to baseline a repo to pick up updates.
- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- git-github-advanced: Git/GitHub procedures beyond the baseline lifecycle. Use for commit layering, recovering a branch after a squash-merge, CI-trigger rules, GitHub Actions gotchas, or merge-relocation traps.
- merge-to-main: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.
- writing-claudinite-skills: Authoring or changing a skill in the Claudinite corpus — SKILL.md conventions, where a skill's checks and tests live, catalog and pack wiring. Use when creating or editing a pack's skills/<name>/ in the canon; a consumer project's own agent docs are authoring-agent-docs' turf.
- writing-handover-issues: How to write a task list a PERSON will execute — a handover issue, an adoption checklist, a "steps only a human can do" list. Use when filing or editing any issue whose body asks a human to click, set, register or copy something. Not for issues describing work you will do yourself.
- writing-migration-plans: Where a plan and a design live, and how to order a plan's phases so nothing stalls mid-run — the plan is a tracking issue (never a plan document in the repo), the design doc carries only the end state with rationale and alternatives; front-load the out-of-band setup, write ALL the code including the cleanup and take one approval for the stack, then chain every execution step to the verification of the one before it as a queued continuation, size the links (how many PRs, what each one's diff is predicted to touch and the automerge policy that prediction becomes) and write the chain to survive a policy park, a red CI or a PR closed unmerged, and keep the tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use BEFORE writing any DESIGN.md, migration plan, phased implementation plan, rollout or cutover plan — including the moment you are about to create a docs/<initiative>/ file — when asked to run a plan as a chain of ad-hoc tasks, and when working through a plan's tracking issue.
- writing-pack-prose: How pack prose is written — RULES.md rules, SKILL.md bodies and check text in a Claudinite pack, local or canon — brevity, structure, triggerability, findability, and the per-pack references doc that carries each rule's rationale. Use before writing or editing any pack's RULES.md or SKILL.md, or when landing a lesson as prose.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.json or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
